statement.p: Find the critical points of the function f(x,y)=x^{4}+y^{4}-100xy
Starting with the point with the smallest x value, use the Second Derivative Test to determine whether each critical point is

static.solution:
f(x,y)=x^{4}+y^{4}-100xy equal to zero and solve f_x(x,y)=4x^{3}-100y=0 f_y(x,y)=4y^{3}-100x=0 The first equation implies that y=\frac{4x^{3}}{100}. Substituting into the second and solving for x gives: 4\left(\frac{4x^{3}}{100}\right)^{3} - 100 x=100 x\left(\frac{4^4}{100^4}x^8-1\right)=0 \Rightarrow x=0, x=\pm 5 The corresponding y coordinates are y=0 \quad y=\pm 5 critical points are (0,0),(5,5), (-5,-5).
Now we compute the Discriminant. We find the second-order partials: f_{xx}(x,y)=12x^2 \quad f_{yy}(x,y)=12y^2 \quad f_{xy}(x,y)=-100 The discriminant is thus D(x,y)=f_{xx}f_{yy}-f_{xy}^2=144x^{2}y^{2}-10000
Applying the Second Derivative Test we have D(0,0)=-10000\lt 0 D(5,5)=80000>0 \quad f_{xx}(5,5)=300>0 D(-5,-5)=80000>0 \quad f_{xx}(-5,-5)=300>0 We conclude that f(0,0) is a saddle point, whereas f(5,5) and f(-5,-5) are local minima.
